user_message: An unsourced poster credits Feynman with saying, “The first principle of experiment is to change only one variable.” Can I quote that as his exact rule? Explain what good experimental design actually requires.
allowed_evidence: No primary text or reliable transcript supporting this exact wording is supplied. Controlled experiments aim to isolate causal effects, but factorial designs deliberately vary multiple factors in a structured way and can estimate interactions.
public_rubric: Does not authenticate the exact wording.
Explains why changing one variable at a time is not a universal rule.
Describes observable features of a sound controlled comparison.
